Standard methods for flexCountReg models

Source: R/methods.R
flexCountReg-methods.Rd

Methods that make flexCountReg models work like other fitted models in R, including with AIC(), BIC(), confint(), update() and packages that build on these generics.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
terms(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson", "quantile"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

object, x

a model estimated with this package.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods. For fitted() and residuals() of countreg.rp() models, this can include method (see predict.flexCountReg).

parm

a specification of which parameters are to be given confidence intervals, either a vector of numbers or a vector of names. If missing, all parameters are considered.

level

the confidence level required.

type

the type of residuals: "response" (observed minus fitted), "pearson" (divided by the standard deviation implied by the fitted distribution) or "quantile" (randomized quantile residuals of Dunn and Smyth, 1996, which are standard normal when the model is correct). Pearson and quantile residuals are available for countreg() models.

nsim

number of response vectors to simulate.

seed

an optional random seed, as in simulate.

digits

the number of significant digits to print.

Value

coef(): named numeric vector. vcov(): matrix. logLik(): an object of class logLik. nobs(): integer. fitted(), residuals(): numeric vectors. confint(): matrix with lower and upper limits. formula(): the main model formula. terms(): its terms object. simulate(): a data frame with nsim columns.

Details

coef() returns all estimated parameters, including distribution, underreporting, random-parameter and heterogeneity parameters, named as in summary(). vcov() returns the covariance matrix chosen at fit time: Hessian-based, robust (sandwich) or bootstrapped (see the stderr argument of each estimator).

nobs() is the number of rows used in estimation. For panel models (renb(), poisLind.re(), repois(), negmultinom() and countreg.rp() with panel_id), the nobs attribute of logLik(), which BIC() uses, is the number of panels, because the panels are the independent units. With frequency weights (weights), it is the sum of the weights of the rows (or panels), the size of the expanded data.

fitted() and residuals() are for the rows used in estimation (rows with missing values are not included). simulate() draws new responses from the fitted distribution for the same rows; it is available for countreg() models.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
m <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, data = washington_roads,
              family = "NB2", method = "BFGS")
coef(m)
#> (Intercept)      lnaadt    lnlength   ln(alpha) 
#>  -9.2124976   1.1159467   0.7440786  -0.9162318 
confint(m)
#>                   2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -10.0837231 -8.3412721
#> lnaadt        1.0122314  1.2196620
#> lnlength      0.6076579  0.8804992
#> ln(alpha)    -1.3742012 -0.4582624
AIC(m)
#> [1] 2203.92
BIC(m)
#> [1] 2225.176
head(residuals(m, type = "pearson"))
#> [1] -0.8946308  0.7475106  0.2732503 -0.6512653 -0.9049206  0.3294258
sims <- simulate(m, nsim = 2, seed = 1)
# }
